assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mechanistic discovery of incretin physiology and its conversion into therapies that have transformed type 2 diabetes and obesity care; clear, original, and with very large, lasting clinical and societal impact.
assessment.attribution: Holst and Drucker established GLP-1 physiology and biology; Knudsen led the development of long-acting analogues (liraglutide, semaglutide). Mojsov's and Habener's contributions to the GLP-1 sequence and activity are contested in credit narratives, so a three-person split is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation, multiple approved drugs, outcome trials and broad real-world use; timing is highly appropriate.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among Drucker, Holst, Knudsen, Mojsov (and others not credited) is unresolved.
Mix of basic physiology and industrial drug development may be viewed as compound.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of a new intracellular signalling pathway from the endoplasmic reticulum to the nucleus, elucidating how cells sense and respond to protein-folding stress; fundamental, elegant, with relevance to neurodegeneration, diabetes and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori delineated the IRE1/HAC1/XBP1 UPR mechanism in yeast and mammals, a clean two-person configuration; other contributors (e.g., Ron, Shamu) are outside the supplied credit, which I cannot fully weigh.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed over three decades, with a stable interpretation; disease relevance is growing but therapeutic translation is still early, which does not detract from a basic-science prize.
uncertainties: Whether other UPR pioneers deserve inclusion is uncertain from the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of cGAS as the cytosolic DNA sensor and cGAMP as a second messenger, with STING as adaptor; a conceptually new innate-immune pathway with broad implications for infection, autoimmunity, neuroinflammation and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Chen's discovery of cGAS and cGAMP is decisive; Barber's identification of STING is also decisive. Others (Ishikawa, Sun, Wu) were key co-discoverers or trainees in the pathway, and further contributors (e.g., Vance, Hornung) are outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is widely confirmed with many independent laboratories; therapeutic agonists and antagonists are in clinical testing without approvals, so the field is still maturing.
uncertainties: Allocation between cGAS and STING discoverers may be contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineering of T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory leukemia and lymphoma; a new therapeutic modality with major clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain led the design and clinical translation of CD19 CAR-T; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell therapy and TIL/gene-engineered T cells. Other contributors (Eshhar, Kuwana, Finney, Brenner, Gross) are outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and long follow-up, though toxicity, solid-tumour limitation and manufacturing challenges remain. Recognition is plausible and timely.
uncertainties: Origins of chimeric receptors (Eshhar) are not among the credited names.
Late relapse and toxicity data are still evolving.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mechanistic splicing work led to nusinersen, the first effective disease-modifying therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, which changed a lethal paediatric neuromuscular disease and validated antisense therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the SMN2 exon 7 splicing mechanism and Bennett led the antisense chemistry and drug development at Ionis; this two-person credit is coherent. Roles of others (e.g., Hua, Singh, Melki for SMN genetics) are outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with strong long-term clinical evidence, and the approach has extended to other antisense drugs. Timely.
uncertainties: A prize may need to weigh the underlying SMN1 gene discovery separately.
Therapeutic benefit varies with age at treatment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-frequency deep brain stimulation transformed treatment of advanced Parkinson's disease and tremor, and opened the field of neuromodulation; the clinical impact is large and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Benabid's introduction of thalamic and subthalamic high-frequency stimulation is the central contribution; others, such as basal ganglia circuit researchers and clinical collaborators, are not credited here, so a one-person configuration may be an incomplete account.
assessment.maturity: Decades of randomized and observational evidence; the technique is standard care. Mature, though the contribution is a device and surgical method rather than a molecular discovery.
uncertainties: Whether the Committee considers DBS a discovery or invention in the spirit of the will.
Contributions from basal ganglia circuit research may deserve joint recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of the orexin/hypocretin peptides and the link to narcolepsy type 1 gave a molecular basis for sleep-wake regulation, and led to orexin antagonists and agonists.
assessment.attribution: Orexin was identified independently by Sakurai/Yanagisawa and by de Lecea/Kilduff; Mignot identified the canine narcolepsy gene, which links the receptor to the disease. Priority and credit across five names is delicate and I cannot resolve it from the supplied data.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed; orexin receptor antagonists are approved for insomnia, and agonists are in trials. Timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Independent simultaneous discovery makes the allocation contentious.
Treatment translation of agonists is still ongoing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic and mechanistic identification of BCL11A as the repressor of fetal haemoglobin, leading to the first CRISPR-based therapy (exa-cel) for sickle cell disease and beta-thalassaemia; a clear path from human genetics to cure.
assessment.attribution: Orkin and Sankaran defined BCL11A's role; Thein's GWAS work identified the HbF-associated locus. Bauer's enhancer targeting is later. The distinction between mechanism and CRISPR therapeutic may complicate the configuration.
assessment.maturity: Therapy was approved only in 2023, so long-term durability and access remain unproven, making recognition possibly premature.
uncertainties: Durability of benefit and safety beyond a few years are unknown.
Credit relative to CRISPR editing technology and other HbF genetics researchers is unresolved.
